title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook
author: Avery Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard practices for hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance reviews, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and managers who will run feedback and growth cycles. Use this as the canonical reference for process, templates, ownership, and escalation paths.

Scope

- Applies to all full-time and long-term contractor hires (>6 months) at Redwood Inference.
- Covers roles across engineering, product, research, sales, and support.
- Excludes short-term contractors (<6 months) and internship programs (see separate intern handbook).

Key principles

- Candidate experience: timely communication, transparent expectations, and respectful scheduling.
- Hiring for growth: prioritize demonstrated problem solving, collaboration, and learning ability.
- Manager enablement: give managers clear steps, templates, and decision criteria.

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)

Owner: hiring manager (primary), people-ops (partner). Time-to-fill target: 45 days for IC roles, 60 days for senior/lead roles.

Stages (standardized):

1. Requisition approval
   - Manager opens a requisition in Workday/Greenhouse with role summary, level, compensation range, and required approvals.
   - People-ops verifies compensation band and headcount availability within 2 business days.

2. Job posting & sourcing
   - People-ops posts the role on company careers page and marketplace.
   - Manager and recruiting coordinate on sourcing plan (internal referrals, outbound, agency if needed).

3. Screen (30-minute)
   - Quick technical/functional screen by senior IC or recruiter. Use standardized screen rubric.

4. Interview loop (1-3 technical rounds + 1 cross-functional loop)
   - Each interviewer uses the standardized rubric and records notes in Greenhouse within 24 hours.

5. Debrief & decision
   - Hiring manager runs a decision meeting within 48 hours of final interview. Consensus required from at least 3 interviewers or escalation to hiring director.

6. Offer & negotiation
   - People-ops drafts the offer including equity and signing bonus (if applicable). Manager approves compensation within band. Target offer acceptance within 5 business days of decision.

7. Background checks & onboarding kickoff
   - Offer contingent on background check completion. People-ops schedules the new-hire orientation and manager kickoff.

Interview rubrics and evaluator guidance

- Use the company rubric for role family (engineering/product/sales). Rubric dimensions: core skills, system design (if applicable), collaboration & communication, ownership & impact, learning ability.
- Interviewers must provide: score (1-5), 3 evidence bullets, hiring recommendation (yes/maybe/no).
- Conflict of interest: if an interviewer has direct personal relationship with candidate, disclose and recuse from decision.

Minimum interviewers and pass criteria

- IC roles: 3 interviewers (technical, cross-functional, manager).
- Senior roles: 5 interviewers including a peer, a cross-functional partner, and an engineering/program leader.
- Offer requires at least two "yes" votes and no more than one explicit "no" from senior interviewers; ties escalate to director.

2) New-hire onboarding (day 0 to 90)

Owner: manager (primary), people-ops (coordination), IT (access provisioning).

Onboarding goals:
- Day 1: new hire has laptop, account access, and first-week plan.
- Day 30: contributor on-team tasks, understands codebase and primary systems.
- Day 90: independent ownership of at least one small project and clear growth objectives.

Standard 30/60/90 plan (template)

- Days 0-7: Orientation and setup
  - Complete HR forms and benefits enrollment.
  - Security training and MFA setup.
  - Team introduction and buddy assignment.

- Days 8-30: Ramp up
  - Shadow key processes, run basic ops or code tasks, and attend product/architecture overviews.
  - Weekly 1:1 with manager to track blockers.

- Days 31-90: Ownership and feedback
  - Deliver first independent project.
  - Collect 360 feedback from peers and cross-functional partners at 90 days.

Access and provisioning checklist (owners in parentheses):

- Laptop & device enrollment (IT)
- GitHub/org access (engineering platforms)
- Slack channels & groups (manager)
- Cloud project and infra access (eng-infra; request via terraform-requests)
- Payment & payroll setup (finance)

Onboarding metrics (people-ops):
- 95% of new hires have accounts provisioned by end of day 1.
- 90% of new hires complete required compliance training by day 7.
- 80% of hires reach 90-day goals by day 90 (tracked via manager sign-off).

3) Performance & feedback cycles

Cadence:
- Continuous feedback: managers are expected to have weekly 1:1s and ad-hoc coaching.
- Formal check-ins: 30- and 90-day check-ins for new hires (manager + people-ops).
- Quarterly check-ins: goal review and calibration discussions.
- Annual performance review: calibrated across org, impacts compensation and promotion cycles.

Performance rating scale (example):

- Exceeds Expectations (EE)
- Meets Expectations (ME)
- Below Expectations (BE)

Manager responsibilities in reviews:

- Collect feedback from peers and stakeholders at least 7 days before the review.
- Document evidence and examples tied to objectives and core competencies.
- Calibrate with peer managers during calibration window.
- Discuss development plan and compensation implications with people-ops before issuing final rating.

Promotion & level change process

1. Manager prepares a promotion packet: justification, evidence, impact, peer comparisons.
2. People-ops reviews compensation banding and equity implications.
3. Cross-functional calibration panel reviews and signs off.
4. HR and finance finalize offer/comp package for new level.

4) Feedback culture & difficult conversations

- Use the SBI model (Situation-Behavior-Impact) for structured feedback.
- For performance improvement plans (PIP): PIP should be used only when coaching and incremental steps have not produced measurable improvement. People-ops must be engaged before a PIP is issued.
- Escalation path for unresolved manager-employee issues: people-ops partner -> head of people -> legal (if termination or sensitive).

5) Manager playbook: practical checklists

New manager first 30 days:
- Read manager onboarding packet and complete manager training in LMS.
- Schedule recurring 1:1s with direct reports.
- Run career conversations: understand aspirations for each direct report.
- Set team priorities and a 90-day plan.

Hiring checklist for managers:
- Create clear role spec and success criteria (measureable outcomes).
- Assemble interview loop and assign interview leads.
- Ensure rubrics are attached to Greenhouse interview slots.

Performance check-in template (used in the HRIS):
- Objectives review (OKRs / team goals)
- Recent accomplishments and examples
- Areas for growth and support needed
- Next steps and owner for each action

6) Templates & artifacts (links)

- Job description template (link placeholder)
- Offer letter template (comp + equity guideline)
- 30/60/90 plan template (link placeholder)

Related resources

- See the manager-training course in LMS for role-based leadership content.

Closing notes
This playbook is intended to be a living document. People-ops will review annually and after any major org changes. For process exceptions (e.g., headcount freezes, urgent hires), contact your people-ops partner directly for expedited approvals.
